open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM`; otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it is malformed
open_points.question: What exact lexical grammar and numeric ranges make the two camera fields and the offset usable, and does an invalid offset invalidate `DateTimeOriginal` or merely cause that time to use the configured zone?
options: Accept only the EXIF date-time grammar and a specified offset range; an invalid offset is ignored and `DateTimeOriginal` uses the configured zone
Accept other parseable date-time spellings and offsets supported by the chosen library
Treat a present but invalid offset as making `DateTimeOriginal` unusable and continue with EXIF `DateTime`
open_points.default_guess: Accept only `YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS`, require a real UTC offset in the stated shape, and ignore an invalid offset while interpreting an otherwise valid `DateTimeOriginal` in `Europe/Madrid`.

witness.initial: A source has `DateTimeOriginal` `2026:11:18 12:00:00`, `OffsetTimeOriginal` `+25:00`, a different usable EXIF `DateTime`, and a modification time within 24 hours.
events: The owner selects the source for placement.
The deliverer derives the photo moment.
outcomes: The invalid offset is ignored and `DateTimeOriginal` is interpreted in the configured time zone.
The invalid offset makes `DateTimeOriginal` unusable, so the different EXIF `DateTime` supplies the moment.
witness.observer: The calling flow and Portal observe different `photo_date` values.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is `DateTime`.
open_points.question: Which time-zone database and version define `Europe/Madrid`, and what happens when those rules are unavailable?
options: Use the host operating system's time-zone database
Pin and ship a particular time-zone database with the service
Use the host database but refuse startup if `Europe/Madrid` cannot be loaded
open_points.default_guess: Use the system zoneinfo database and refuse service startup if `Europe/Madrid` cannot be loaded.

witness.initial: Two deployments have different time-zone database versions whose rules disagree for a future Europe/Madrid instant; the file modification time makes the camera value otherwise usable.
events: The camera records a local `DateTimeOriginal` without an offset.
The same source is placed on each deployment.
outcomes: The older database converts the local time using its older offset rule.
The newer database converts it using its revised offset rule.
witness.observer: The calling flow and Portal receive different UTC photo dates from identical input.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: Both subfolders stay inside the root.
open_points.question: Must `invoice_subfolder` resolve strictly below the resolved root just like `photo_subfolder`, including at startup, or is its lexical relative-path validation sufficient because this service does not use it?
options: Resolve and validate both subfolders strictly below the root and refuse startup otherwise
Apply resolved containment only to the photo subfolder; validate the invoice subfolder lexically
Permit an invalid invoice subfolder only while the connection is unconfirmed
open_points.default_guess: Resolve both subfolders and refuse startup unless each is strictly below the resolved root.

witness.initial: A confirmed connection has a valid photo subfolder and an `invoice_subfolder` that is a relative path without `..` but is a symbolic link to a directory outside the root.
outcomes: Startup is refused because the invoice folder does not stay inside the root.
Startup succeeds because A5 gives a resolved-path check only for the photo folder.
witness.observer: The operator observes whether the service starts.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no rounding, written in ISO 8601 form.
open_points.question: What exact ISO 8601 spelling must be written, including the date-time separator and whether six fractional digits are always present?
options: Use the language's default ISO formatter, which may omit a zero fractional part
Write a space separator rather than `T` while retaining six fractional digits
open_points.default_guess: Always write `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff` with no offset or `Z` suffix.

witness.initial: The clock returns naive UTC `2026-11-18 12:34:56.000000`, and a fresh publication mark is created.
events: The calling flow records the publication.
witness.observer: A state-file reader, reload, or serialized mark consumer sees different representations.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: INV-13: a counting clock is read exactly once by each of scan, placement and mark and not at all by the health answer (`test_each_operation_reads_the_clock_once`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
open_points.question: Which execution paths must the INV-13 tests exercise to show the invariant and the normative zero-or-one-read rules?
options: Test accepted calls, every pre-clock refusal with zero reads, representative post-clock refusals with one read, replayed marks with one read, and health with zero reads
Test only one successful scan, placement and mark plus health
Test all routes only for the upper bound of one read, without asserting the specified zero-versus-one timing
open_points.default_guess: Require tests for successful calls, all validation stages before the clock, representative refusals after the clock, replayed marks, and health, while asserting no path reads more than once.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text: Any known vulnerability listed for an installed version blocks the deployment, whatever its severity
open_points.question: Which OSV records count as a known vulnerability listed for an installed version, particularly a record marked withdrawn or carrying conflicting affected-version data?
options: Apply OSV semantics and ignore withdrawn records; block only when the snapshot's effective affected ranges include the installed version
Block whenever any record names the installed version, including withdrawn records
Treat a withdrawn or internally inconsistent matching record as a check that cannot complete, so deployment does not pass
open_points.default_guess: Follow OSV record semantics, ignore withdrawn records, and fail the check closed when the remaining record data cannot determine whether the installed version is affected.

witness.initial: The deployment image contains a particular Pillow version, and the accepted OSV snapshot contains a record naming that version but marked withdrawn.
events: The deployment route checks every installed distribution against the snapshot.
The route decides whether the image may deploy.
outcomes: The withdrawn record is ignored and the deployment may proceed if no active record matches.
The record is still a listed known vulnerability, so deployment is blocked.
witness.observer: The deployer observes whether the image is accepted.
